rows.observationText: The operators on the swage press have been issued gloves and told to keep their hands clear, and the two-hand control on the press has been strapped down with tape.

rawProposal.observationInterpretation: The observation identifies an active machine guarding hazard where a safety device (two-hand control) on a swage press has been deliberately bypassed/strapped down with tape, and administrative measures (verbal instruction and PPE) are inappropriately relied upon instead of an effective engineering control.

evidence.quotedText: the two-hand control on the press has been strapped down with tape.

hazardCandidates.conditionRationale: The engineering control designed to protect operators' hands (the two-hand control) is explicitly documented as compromised and bypassed ('strapped down with tape'). Administrative instructions and gloves do not replace or render a bypassed point-of-operation control controlled.
hazardCandidates.independentHazardRationale: This is the single machine guarding hazard identified on the swage press involving bypassed point-of-operation safeguarding.

correctiveActionIntent.objective: Restore and maintain the point-of-operation safeguarding by removing tape from the two-hand control and ensuring it functions properly to prevent operation with hands in the danger zone.

rows.observationText: The missing floor plate at the end of the mezzanine walkway was raised in the morning briefing and the crew were told to step around it.

rawProposal.observationInterpretation: The observation identifies a missing floor plate on an elevated mezzanine walkway, presenting a hole and fall hazard. Although discussed in a morning briefing with instructions to step around it, verbal administrative warnings do not physically eliminate or control the opening, leaving an active hazard.

evidence.quotedText: missing floor plate at the end of the mezzanine walkway
the crew were told to step around it

hazardCandidates.conditionRationale: A physical opening exists due to a missing floor plate on a mezzanine walkway. Instructing personnel to step around an open hazard is an administrative warning and does not constitute an effective physical control (such as a cover or guardrail), meaning the condition remains active.
hazardCandidates.independentHazardRationale: This is the single physical condition described in the observation.

correctiveActionIntent.objective: Install a secure, load-bearing cover or replace the missing floor plate to protect workers on the mezzanine walkway from tripping and falling through the opening.
